name: New Genre
tagline: International brand-and-build studio with 24 published case studies
description: An international multi-disciplinary studio of designers, developers and strategists that sells four service lines: Strategy (naming, brand architecture, brand voice, ideation sprints), Design (visual identities, design systems, UI/UX, art direction, 3D, motion, print, iconography), Development (React, Next.js, Svelte, Webflow, WordPress, CMS, e-commerce, integrations, auditing) and Growth & Evolution (brand activations, campaigns, events, OOH, packaging, merch). The work page carries 24 case studies, including ElevenLabs, Accel, Sylvera, SigmaOS, Gravity Sketch, Knotel, Bite Back and Ello, each tagged Strategy / Design / Development / Experience. The about page names 11 team members. No prices, founding date, or office location are published.
agent_guidance: Reach for this as visual precedent when a user is branding an AI or climate-tech company and wants proof of how identity, motion and site build hold together across one system — the ElevenLabs, Sylvera, Overmind and SigmaOS case studies are the strongest of the 24. Prefer it over a pure branding studio when the ask spans naming through shipped front end, since it states React, Next.js, Svelte, Webflow and WordPress delivery in one place. It publishes no rates, no process phases and no downloadable assets, so do not quote costs or timelines from it, and do not repeat the "world's most disruptive thinkers" line — that is the studio's own marketing copy, not a verified claim.
why_it_matters: A rare studio that shows brand strategy and production front-end work on the same case studies, with a client roster (ElevenLabs, Accel, Sylvera) that makes the standard credible.
notable_for: brand strategy through shipped front end
names its build stack: React, Next, Svelte, Webflow
tier_reason: Actively-maintained studio site with 24 enumerated case studies and a verifiable client roster (ElevenLabs, Accel, Sylvera) spanning brand strategy through shipped React/Next front end, but it exposes no registry, API, or reusable assets, so it stays below S.
